title: A redline of a 2x screenshot reads in points, with dimension lines a designer reads at a glance
goal: Measurements on a Retina screenshot say their numbers in points ("124 pt" for a button 248 pixels wide) instead of a "px" that reads as wrong, and each dimension line shows plainly what it spans, so a redline Ask makes reads as a finished spec rather than a tangle.
notes: Carried over from measuring-a-ui-gives-a-calm-redline-each-kind-of (2026-10-20), which shipped code-chosen marks and clear readout placement (Sources/PhotonzCore/Redline.swift, find_measurements / mark_measurements) and took the settings case from 32.5 to 59.0 for Ask (judge 2.8 to 4.8). What the judge still says, verbatim, from Scripts/ask-eval.sh run --engine ask --cases settings-measurements (runs 20261021-044351-ask, 20261021-044837-ask, 20261021-050243-ask or the latest): "values don't match what they point at (124 px on a roughly 250 px button, 18 px on a gap that is clearly larger)"; "there are no end ticks to show what is being measured"; "the brackets don't clearly mark what they measure (26 px, 30 px, 17 px)". The 124 is right in points (MeasureUnit.points, logical px) but labelled px: MeasureUnit.suffix is "px" for both units by design (Measure.swift line 12). Only three call sites use the suffix (Measure.swift label/chipText, MeasureSizeGroup.swift:176, DocumentUnit.swift:27) but about 46 test files and 38 walks expect px readouts, which is why it did not fit in the redline task. Size brackets are MeasureSizeGroup + caliper extension lines (MeasurePlan.swift, MeasureRasterizer.swift).
acceptance: On a 2x screenshot every measurement readout and the Measurements list say pt unless the person chose pixels, and every walk and test that expected px on a 2x picture is updated in the same change
A dimension line shows where it starts and stops (end ticks or the Measure tool's equivalent), so a judge or a person can tell what each number spans
The settings measurements case scores 8 or more on clean and aligned in the eval for Ask and for the skill (Scripts/ask-eval.sh run --cases settings-measurements)

A person placing many measurements by hand gets readouts kept off words, controls and other measurement lines the way an Ask redline does, without undoing the leash and on-the-line choices the user already made (MeasureCalloutClearanceTests, MeasureLabelPlacementTests)

log.note: owns no walks; the ones it names are examples
